Fish.Description: Ascent to Schellschlicht – A steep path, which must now be followed with great caution, as the terrain is crumbly and drops away steeply
Ascent to Madonna – Somewhat exposed, but not particularly difficult
Ascent to Dürnbachwand – Challenging and strenuous steep climb with a few exposed sections and risk of falling

Ascent to Frieder – The eastern approach includes several exposed sections. Toward the end, the trail fades away, giving way to a very steep, rocky ascent, where snowfields may still be present in late spring
Ascent to Wasserwand – The rocky neighbor of Heuberg is reached via an exposed via ferrata, where absolute surefootedness and a head for heights are essential for the short iron path

Ascent to Kindlwand – A rocky summit, known for its small passage cave that serves as the approach to the top, with the final ascent requiring surefootedness, a head for heights, and some easy climbing
Ascent to Gedererwand from the North – Steep ascent on an unmarked trail through forest and scree with a short key gully below the Zwölferturm, requiring good route-finding and surefootedness
Descent from Friedenrath – Very steep with snow patches possible in spring due to north-facing slope
Sonnenbergrat – An exposed ridge that can be extremely dangerous when snowfields linger into late spring
Ascent to Kofel – Includes some steeper sections with steel ropes and can be crowded on weekends
Ascent to Gartnerwand – Very steep with exposed climbing sections, partially secured by steel ropes
Ascent to Fleischbank – The final ascent over the summit ridge is partly airy, surefootedness and a head for heights are required
Ascent to Burgberger Hörnle – Steep, strenous climb with exposed sections that demand sure footing
Ascent to Birkkarpitze – Long, demanding alpine climb through rugged terrain and exposed ridges
Descent via Gjaidsteig – Requires surefootedness and a head for heights as well as a good portion of fitness
Mountain ridge along Hochplatte – The narrow ridge demands steady footing and a head for heights
Descent via Falzsteig from Watzmannhaus – Some passages are secured with steel ropes on steep rock
Ascent from Soiernsee to Soiernscharte – The long, loose scree slope tests endurance and balance
Ascent to Stuiben – A very long ladder must be climbed, requiring no fear of heights
Ascent to Lachenspitze – The final rocky approach requires careful climbing
Descent from Pyramidenspitze – Slippery gravel sections make the way down tricky
Descent from Entschenkopf – Sections with steel ropes run right next to a cliff where fatal falls have happened
Ascent via Alpgartensteig – Steep stairs lead up exposed terrain
Ascent to Große Klammspitze – The path narrows to demanding ridge terrain near the top
Geigelstein to Mühlhörndl – The little-used path is overgrown and way finding is difficult
Ascent to Schindertor – The final rock gate must be climbed using only metal steps without ropes
Ascent to Brünnstein – Many rope-secured passages, exposed but not too severe
Mountain ridge along Kampen peaks – The exposed ridge offers little margin for error
Ascent to Attaviros – Extremely steep rock terrain, way marked only by red dots, with fog often complicating orientation
Ascent to Ettaler Manndl – A very steep rocky section with many ropes to hold on to
Ascent to Daniel – The final rocky approach requires careful climbing
Bayernsteig – Officially closed since Nov 2024 due to lack of maintenance and unsafe conditions
Descent to Ehrwald – Extremely steep with unstable loose gravel, making footing treacherous
Ascent towards Blankenstein – The final approach is steep and covered with loose stones
Ascent to Hochstaufen – Involves a bit of climbing and ropes
Ascent Hörndl via Jägersteig – Steep and with ropes
Acent to Guffert – The northern ascent is partly equipped with wire ropes and includes some exposed sections
Ascent to Brecherspitz – The final ridge is narrow, exposed, and can be slippery, requiring surefootedness despite the otherwise moderate trail
Coburger Bank – Short but steep path over rocky, exposed terrain that requires a bit of scrambling
Descent from Meilerhütte – Over long, loose scree fields, demanding careful footing and strong knees
Descent via Köppelsteig – Difficult, solitary trail requiring absolute surefootedness and a good head for heights
Cachoeira Fumaça to Lençóis – Extremely long, poorly marked trail with river crossings and rugged terrain, demanding navigation skills and lots of endurance
Lençóis to Caeté-Açu – Long, rugged trail with overgrown and exposed sections, river crossings, poor signage, no cell coverage, and a hot, shade-free finish
Descent from Kurktrekkersnek – Very steep and partly overgrown
Ascent to Roßstein – Path partially secured with wire ropes
Wolfsschlucht – Several steep sections and steel cable passages
Descent from Halserspitz – Very steep, demanding balance and no fear of heights
Coburger Bank – Short but steep path over rocky, exposed terrain that requires a bit of scrambling
Descent to Ehrwald via Knappensteig – Over long, loose scree fields, demanding careful footing and strong knees
Brannenburger Steig – A few steeper sections when ascending Wendelstein
Ascent to Penha de Águia – Very steep and can be slippery after rain
Descent from Gaisalphorn – Exposed ridge with some tricky sections, which, however, have mostly been made safer by steel cables and a three-meter ladder
